nodes.title: Auxiliary PEL height lattice
nodes.statement: The height labels of the distinguished auxiliary PEL local factor form Lambda = {(a,b) in Z squared : 2 divides a+b}, with componentwise addition. Quaternionic height m embeds as (m,m). The difference character (a,b) maps to (a-b)/2; its kernel in Lambda is the diagonal and it identifies Lambda modulo the diagonal with Z. Both coordinates are half the corresponding relative quasi-isogeny heights, in the conventions of BZ (5.13) and (5.23).
hypotheses: K is a finite extension of Q_p, with integers O, uniformizer pi, residue field k of size q, and completed maximal unramified extension Kcheck. Formal and rigid carriers are imported, not supplied by an algebraic scheme carrier.
Use the polarized paired q0 and conjugate-q0 factors of BZ, with the BZ framing arrow Y_bar to X_bar. These two integer labels are not absolute p-heights.
proofSteps: Use the polarization relation to impose parity of the two half-heights.
Apply the height translations in BZ (5.15) to identify the components with the height-zero component times Lambda.
Check the diagonal embedding in (6.39). For the quotient description, use a-b even; (r,-r) maps to r and zero difference forces a=b.
acceptance: (1,0) is excluded; (1,-1) is included.
The diagonal contains negative heights and is a proper subgroup of Lambda.

sources.match: Parity-constrained labels of the auxiliary local RZ factor and the diagonal quaternionic inclusion; the difference-character quotient is an elementary consequence.

api.name: PelHeightLattice.mem
api.statement: A pair (a,b) is in Lambda exactly when 2 divides a+b.

api.name: PelHeightLattice.add
api.statement: Lambda is closed under componentwise addition, contains zero and is closed under negation, agreeing with the existing additive-subgroup vocabulary.

api.name: PelHeightLattice.diagonal
api.statement: For every m in Z, (m,m) is in Lambda; the map is injective and additive.

api.name: PelHeightLattice.difference
api.statement: On Lambda the integer (a-b)/2 is additive, surjective and has kernel the diagonal.

tests.name: PelHeightLattice.oddPair

tests.name: PelHeightLattice.oppositePair
tests.statement: (1,-1) is permitted and has difference character 1; using only the diagonal fails.

tests.name: PelHeightLattice.negativeDiagonal
tests.statement: (-1,-1) is permitted and has difference zero; using nonnegative heights fails.

tests.name: PelHeightLattice.translation
tests.statement: Adding (1,1) preserves Lambda and the difference character; changing only one coordinate by 1 does not preserve Lambda.

nodes.title: Very free action on Drinfeld charts
nodes.statement: For the effective projective arithmetic group Gamma acting on the imported Bruhat–Tits tree T, call the action very free when every gamma different from 1 and every vertex x satisfy d_T(x,gamma x)>2, where d_T counts edges. The light predicate also makes sense for an actual group action on a set equipped with a specified integer-valued distance. In the geometric use this distance must be the tree distance. This is a sufficient chart-separation condition, stronger than an action free on vertices.
hypotheses: K is a finite extension of Q_p, with integers O, uniformizer pi, residue field k of size q, and completed maximal unramified extension Kcheck. Formal and rigid carriers are imported, not supplied by an algebraic scheme carrier.
Gamma is the image in PGL2(K), after removing the scalar kernel, of the determinant-valuation-zero arithmetic stabilizer. In the geometric theorem Gamma is discrete and cocompact.
proofSteps: Import the tree, its action and edge-count distance from ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2.
Apply BC Part III 5.3.1 to the effective arithmetic group and retain the strict bound greater than 2.
Shrinking the tame level eliminates the finitely many short displacement classes in a compact fundamental domain; the arithmetic smallness argument is part of the quotient theorem.
acceptance: A translation by 2 on an integer line acts freely but fails this condition.
Central scalars must be removed before imposing this condition.

sources.match: Strict displacement greater than two allows standard formal vertex charts to descend and glue.

api.name: VeryFreeChartAction.distance
api.statement: For an actual group action, the condition is the universal strict displacement bound greater than 2.

api.name: VeryFreeChartAction.free
api.statement: If d(x,x)=0, the condition excludes every nonidentity vertex stabilizer.

api.name: VeryFreeChartAction.subgroup
api.statement: Restriction to a subgroup preserves the condition with the induced action and the same distance.

api.name: VeryFreeChartAction.conjugation
api.statement: Conjugating Gamma by a tree isometry preserves the condition; the distance is transported by that isometry.

tests.name: VeryFreeChartAction.trivialGroup
tests.statement: The trivial group satisfies the predicate for every vertex set; requiring the bound for the identity would fail.

tests.name: VeryFreeChartAction.translationThree
tests.statement: On the integer line with edge distance |x-y|, n acts by x maps to x+3n; every nonzero n has displacement at least 3.

tests.name: VeryFreeChartAction.translationTwo
tests.statement: The free action n:x maps to x+2n fails: n=1 has displacement 2.

tests.name: VeryFreeChartAction.fixedVertex
tests.statement: An action with a nonidentity element fixing a vertex fails even if other orbits have long displacement.

nodes.title: Separated Drinfeld quotient charts
nodes.statement: Let Gamma be a discrete cocompact subgroup of PGL2(K) acting very freely on T. The standard Drinfeld vertex charts descend to the quotient formal curve Gamma backslash OmegaHat and glue with their original edge overlap charts. Its special fibre has one P1_k for each vertex orbit and one ordinary node of thickness 1 for each unoriented edge orbit. The quotient map is injective on each radius-one vertex neighbourhood in the tree. There is a proper algebraic curve model whose completion is this formal quotient, with smooth rigid generic fibre Gamma backslash Omega; regularity and semistability follow from the original charts. Each normalized rational component has q+1 distinct attaching points, so the special fibre is stable.
hypotheses: K is a finite extension of Q_p, with integers O, uniformizer pi, residue field k of size q, and completed maximal unramified extension Kcheck. Formal and rigid carriers are imported, not supplied by an algebraic scheme carrier.
The effective Gamma action satisfies VeryFreeChartAction; import the formal quotient gluing and proper algebraisation supplier. This theorem uses no general finite-stabilizer quotient assertion.
proofSteps: If two vertices in one radius-one ball were identified, a nonidentity translate would move a vertex by at most two. Use very freeness to rule this out.
Glue the actual BC Part I charts along edge charts, then take a finite fundamental domain for cocompactness; obtain properness and use the requested algebraisation theorem.

Read the local equations xy=pi, identify component and node orbits, and count the q+1 distinct branches on each normalized P1. Since q is at least 2, every rational component has at least three special points.
acceptance: The chart theorem is sufficient under very freeness; mere vertex freeness is not used as the chart hypothesis.
No assertion of regularity survives arbitrary ramified base change: xy=pi becomes xy=u times pi_L^e.
The unramified local charts have thickness one.

sources.match: Standard vertex and edge charts and the sufficient smallness condition for gluing their quotient.
The blow-up union has reduced tree-indexed rational components and original node charts.

nodes.title: Local factors of the auxiliary quaternionic PEL space
nodes.statement: For the precise BZ auxiliary PEL datum and chosen compatible framing object, the distinguished local RZ functor is OmegaHat_K over O_Kcheck times Lambda. The other p_i local RZ functors, with their prescribed rigidifications, are constant sheaves Gbullet_pi/Kbullet_pi, after the choice (5.7). Thus the global local factor is the product of the distinguished factor and these discrete coset factors. On (omega,(a,b)), a framing quasi-isogeny (delta1,delta2) acts by (pr(delta1)omega,(a+ord det delta1,b+ord det delta2)), with scalar-product constraint delta1 delta2 in K times. The corrected Weil datum in BZ Theorem 6.3 translates the distinguished labels by (1,1); its conversion to the theorem’s inverse base automorphism is right multiplication by Pi inverse on the finite-adelic factor.
hypotheses: K is a finite extension of Q_p, with integers O, uniformizer pi, residue field k of size q, and completed maximal unramified extension Kcheck. Formal and rigid carriers are imported, not supplied by an algebraic scheme carrier.

F is totally real; B is split at exactly one real place tau and division at v above p. Bcheck exchanges the invariants at tau and v and agrees elsewhere. Use the BZ auxiliary CM extension, hermitian datum, embeddings and local-level restrictions (6.29)–(6.31), not an arbitrary PEL datum.

Distinguished level is maximal and its multiplier subgroup is O_K units; other local factors obey BZ (4.6) and (6.31). Preserve the polarization classes and rigidifications in Definitions 5.3 and 5.6.
proofSteps: Use the strict special-formal-module representability already owned by /drinfeld-representability. Apply BZ Lemma 5.10 and Proposition 5.11 to the distinguished polarized factor; label it with /pel-height-lattice.
For each other p_i, transport the rigidification to the chosen constant etale framing group and its multiplicative dual; BZ Proposition 5.4 identifies the functor with its coset sheaf.
Compute both heights after the central correction in (6.16), as in Theorem 6.3. Keep this arithmetic datum separate from the normalized framing-group action.
acceptance: The auxiliary factor is not just OmegaHat times one height integer.
The discrete other-prime factors cannot be omitted when F has several primes above p.
Switching BC and BZ framing arrows inverts the quasi-isogeny; do not carry the same height sign across both conventions.

nodes.title: Quaternionic transfer from basic PEL uniformisation
nodes.statement: At maximal division-prime level and the other p-adic levels of BZ (6.31), the formal quaternionic uniformisation map factors through the selected open-and-closed quaternionic components of the auxiliary PEL model of Definition 6.5 and is an isomorphism onto those components. The inclusion on local labels is m maps to (m,m). The rational automorphism group inclusion is controlled by the exact central sequence 1 to F times to Bcheck times times L times to I(Q) to 1, where L/F is the auxiliary CM extension, with kernel c maps to (c,c inverse). After a cofinal tame shrinking, the induced quotient inclusion is open and closed and hits every selected component. Transporting the PEL uniformisation and its corrected twist gives the quaternionic formal completion with right Pi-inverse descent, compatibly with tame Hecke correspondences. This division-prime proof route does not use Carayol's split-place connected comparison.
hypotheses: K is a finite extension of Q_p, with integers O, uniformizer pi, residue field k of size q, and completed maximal unramified extension Kcheck. Formal and rigid carriers are imported, not supplied by an algebraic scheme carrier.

F is totally real; B is split at exactly one real place tau and division at v above p. Bcheck exchanges the invariants at tau and v and agrees elsewhere. Use the BZ auxiliary CM extension, hermitian datum, embeddings and local-level restrictions (6.29)–(6.31), not an arbitrary PEL datum.
Choose auxiliary CM/tame levels as in BZ Definition 6.5 and (6.31). Retain the central kernel and all components of the selected canonical quaternionic tower.

The basic PEL uniformisation of BZ Proposition 6.2, including deformation-theoretic etaleness, polarized Hasse-principle surjectivity and Weil equivariance, is a supplier contract, not a consequence of PEL representability or complex uniformisation.
proofSteps: Identify Bcheck using (6.22) and compute the central exact sequence by Hilbert 90. In Proposition 6.6 the torus L times/F times is anisotropic at infinity; shrink the auxiliary level using the finite relevant unit classes and the congruence argument so that no extra CM translate identifies two quaternionic points.
Insert /auxiliary-pel-local-factors into Proposition 6.2, then use the diagonal height embedding (6.39) and Proposition 6.6 to obtain an open-and-closed immersion of the arithmetic formal quotients.

Follow the proof of Theorem 6.7: take compatible special-fibre points over a cofinal system of levels, use properness to choose a compatible framing, and use Hecke transitivity to meet every selected component. Open-and-closed immersion plus surjectivity gives the isomorphism.
Convert the corrected PEL Weil datum using Theorem 6.3; the quaternionic formula is id on OmegaHat and right multiplication by Pi inverse on the adelic quotient, together with tau_c=Spf(tau inverse).
acceptance: A geometric component isomorphism alone does not prove surjectivity onto all canonical components.
A raw inclusion of Bcheck times in I(Q) is insufficient without the inverse-diagonal central kernel.
The division-prime theorem is independent of the unresolved arbitrary-ramification YZ determinant repair.

nodes.title: Split-place comparison and its finite-level fields
nodes.statement: For Carayol's split finite-place quaternionic and auxiliary PEL towers, with the fixed neutral-component identifications and sufficiently small compatible tame levels, Proposition 4.4.3 gives an isomorphism of level-zero neutral components and their O_p-linear p-divisible groups over F_p^nr, equivariant for the indicated inclusion of effective extension groups Delta0/SL2(O_p) into Delta0-prime/SL2(O_p). Section 4.5.1 lifts it to the unions of p-power level structures above these level-zero components over F_p^nr. For each finite n, Section 4.5.5 compares the chosen neutral connected components over F_p^n, the abelian extension defined by units congruent to 1 modulo pi^n; n=0 means F_p^nr. The compatible auxiliary tame level can depend on n. Comparison of a full union over F_p^nr and comparison of one selected component over F_p^n are different contracts. No division-prime or all-n common-tame conclusion follows from these split-place statements.
hypotheses: B at p is M2(F_p); use the Carayol determinant, reciprocity and right-Galois-action conventions, and the coefficient-free connected towers.

The finite torsion component field F_p^n corresponds by local class field theory to U_p^n; use Carayol's geometric-Frobenius normalization. Completing the comparison field gives the corresponding completed-field statement, not a descent to a smaller field.
proofSteps: Use the equivariant geometric connected comparison of §4.2 and compare the two extension groups in §§4.3–4.4. The inertia quotient identifies the descent to F_p^nr.
Retain the O_p-linear p-divisible comparison in Proposition 4.4.3. Pass to compatible torsion-trivialization spaces above the neutral level-zero component as in §4.5.1.

Apply the norm-one/tame quotient in §4.5.2 and the neutral-component conclusion of §4.5.5 over its stated F_p^n. Distinguish field of definition from a theorem of minimality of that field, which is not asserted here.
acceptance: The theorem never assumes B_p division.
F_p^0 is F_p^nr; for n positive F_p^n can be ramified over it.
The statement gives an auxiliary level for each fixed n, not one small tame level working uniformly at all n.

nodes.title: Compatible Drinfeld level structures on the uniformized tower
nodes.statement: For sufficiently small tame level in the CDN20 global division-prime setup, pullback of the quaternionic special formal O_D-module under uniformisation agrees, with its action and framing convention, with the universal Drinfeld module. Therefore its finite generic-fibre torsion-level functors are the Drinfeld covers M_n in the CDN congruence convention, and the quotient identifies the entire inverse system Sh_n(U)^an with Bcheck times backslash [M_n times Bcheck(A_f^v) times/U] for n at least 1. These identifications commute with forgetting local level, shrinking tame level and away-v Hecke correspondences. This contract refers to an actual module comparison; unrelated isomorphisms of the base curves do not induce it. It makes no semistability or regularity assertion for all integral higher-level covers.
hypotheses: K is a finite extension of Q_p, with integers O, uniformizer pi, residue field k of size q, and completed maximal unramified extension Kcheck. Formal and rigid carriers are imported, not supplied by an algebraic scheme carrier.

Descend along the effective arithmetic action and compare with CDN Proposition 5.4. Keep rigid generic fibres throughout the higher-level conclusion.

nodes.title: Kurihara graph with lengths for arithmetic quotients
nodes.statement: Let Gamma be a discrete cocompact subgroup of PGL2(K). Form the formal/algebraic Mumford quotient by first using a normal finite-index Schottky subgroup and then its effective finite quotient. Its dual graph with lengths is (Gamma backslash T)*: take orbits of vertices and oriented edges, delete the edge orbits fixed by reversal, and retain loops and repeated edges among the rest. The length of a retained edge is the order of the stabilizer in Gamma of any lifted oriented edge. The algebraic model is normal, proper and flat, its generic fibre is smooth, and its reduced connected special fibre has split ordinary nodes and rational normalizations of components. At an edge of length m the completed local equation is xy=pi^m. Resolution replaces it by a path of m unit-length edges; it preserves cycle homology and the weighted cycle pairing. For positive generic genus, obtaining the minimal regular model also successively contracts rational components of valence one, as in Kurihara Proposition 3-4; valence-two components are not contracted merely for failing stability.
hypotheses: K is a finite extension of Q_p, with integers O, uniformizer pi, residue field k of size q, and completed maximal unramified extension Kcheck. Formal and rigid carriers are imported, not supplied by an algebraic scheme carrier.

Gamma acts effectively in PGL2(K); all oriented-edge stabilizers are finite. Construct the quotient using the actual Drinfeld/Mumford model and a finite-index normal Schottky subgroup. Minimal regular-model statements require generic genus greater than zero.
This is an arithmetic quotient comparison; the generic graph-with-lengths, resolution, Jacobian character lattice and monodromy theorem belong to StableReduction and R11.4.
proofSteps: Use Kurihara Proposition 3-2 to identify components, split branches, length and the local ring. Edge inversions identify two branches and remove that node; BC Part III §5.4.3 explains the deletion.
Use Kurihara Lemma 3-3 for the local finite quotient and the subsequent blow-up description on p.288. A thickness-m edge subdivides to m unit edges after resolving the xy=pi^m singularity.

Apply the existing normalization and regular-model suppliers, then the R11.4 graph/character-lattice theorem. Under subdivision a cycle has the same coefficient on every new segment, hence contributes m times the original edge coefficient product. The generic weighted extension is a recorded supplier gap, not re-owned here.
acceptance: If Gamma is Schottky, there are no reversed fixed edge orbits, stabilizers are trivial and every length is one, recovering /tree-dual-graph.
An inverted edge must disappear; treating it as a retained loop is wrong.
A node of thickness m>1 is not regular and cannot be fed to an unweighted regular-model formula without resolution.

gaps.title: Formal arithmetic quotient and algebraisation
gaps.detail: AdicSpacesPartII:R2 supplies formal and generic-fibre machinery, but no target for the needed separated arithmetic quotient and proper algebraisation was found. Add the precise theorem in AdicSpacesPartII Part II; do not infer algebraisation from Raynaud equivalence alone. This includes effective finite quotients used for nonsmall levels.

gaps.title: Basic PEL uniformisation carrier and hypotheses
gaps.detail: PELModuli:M2 does not currently supply basic RZ uniformisation. Its Part II extension must state BZ Proposition 6.2 for the actual quaternionic auxiliary datum and polarized quasi-isogeny group, including Serre–Tate deformation etaleness, Hasse-principle coverage of all special-fibre points and Weil equivariance. KRZ provides the cited argument in its own unitary setting; no automatic equivalence of that setting with BZ is claimed. Rapoport–Zink Period Spaces, Theorem 6.30, is cited by those sources but was not independently read; it is not in the cleared library.

gaps.title: Compatible universal module at fine levels
gaps.detail: The actual quaternionic universal special formal module and its quotient descent need supplier carriers and the BZ-to-Drinfeld comparison. The target /drinfeld-level-structure-comparison spells out what is needed. One must prove this comparison before deducing higher-level covers from the maximal-level curve theorem; a coarse universal family is not substituted.

This packet plans only the arithmetic identification and records the extension as R11 Part II, without duplicate generic monodromy nodes.
